titre: Yop2D | Free No-Code 2D Game Engine for Android
description: Yop2D is a free, no-code 2D game engine for Android. Create games on your tablet or phone with {nb_noeuds} visual nodes, physics, tilemaps and animations, then export an APK offline. No ads, no watermark.
bandeau: This site is available in English
slogan: A free, no-code 2D game engine to create your games directly on Android, on a tablet or a phone.
note_installation: ⚠️ Installation note: the APK is downloaded outside the Play Store, so Android may show a "Play Protect" or "Unknown app" warning. Tap More details, then Install anyway. Yop2D is also in closed testing on Google Play: become a tester. Requires Android 7.0 or newer.
langues_interface: Interface, help and guides in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Japanese
vitrine: Yop2D home screen with the project list, example games and export buttons
Projects & Export

From the home screen, find your projects with their thumbnails and open the example games to learn quickly. With a single button, Yop2D builds your game into a standalone APK file, directly on your device: no computer, no server, no third-party tool.
Yop2D Templates tab: small beginner projects sorted by category
37 templates to learn

In the "Templates" tab, Yop2D asks "What game do you want to make?": 37 small projects that each show one single thing (moving, jumping, shooting, pathfinding, a variable, a HUD, a pause, particles…), sorted by category. Each template works right away and explains on screen which node does what. At the very top, the "Your first game in 5 minutes" guide takes you through it step by step.
Built-in Yop2D library: animated characters, enemies, objects, floors, backgrounds, sounds, music and fonts
A library that has everything

To make your first game you don't need to look anywhere else: the library is already inside Yop2D. Animated characters and enemies, objects, floors and platforms, backgrounds, buttons, sound effects, music, fonts and ready-made titles: in one tap, the image lands in your game with all its animations (idle, walk, jump…). Online packs (Pirates, Space, Hologram interface, Special effects, Plane, Monsters, Touch gestures) are added with a single button, and everything is free to use.
Yop2D visual scene editor on an Android tablet
Visual Level Editor

An interface inspired by professional engines, designed for touch screens. Tap an object to select it, drag to scroll the scene, and use the handles to move, resize or rotate it. Hide or lock any object with one tap so nothing gets moved by accident.
Yop2D tilemap editor: painting a level tile by tile
Tile-Based Levels
Import a tileset, paint your levels tile by tile, and mark once which tiles are solid. Collisions are handled automatically, so platformers and top-down maps are quick to build.
Yop2D animation editor with frame thumbnails and live preview
Real-Time Animation Editor
See your imported frames at a glance and preview your 2D animations in real time, right inside the engine. In game, animations follow pause and slow motion like everything else.
Yop2D styled title with gradient, outline and neon effects
Built-in Titles & Text Effects
Create stylized titles (gradients, outlines, neon, shadows, relief, textures, curves) directly in the engine, instead of making heavy text images in other apps. Your final APK stays light.
Yop2D game text editor, with dialogues in 9 languages
Texts and dialogues in several languages

All the game texts are gathered in a single file that you can edit right inside Yop2D: one line per language (hello.fr, hello.en…). The "Show dialogue" node picks the language of the player's phone by itself: your game speaks 9 languages without any extra node.
Yop2D visual node editor (visual scripting) on a tablet
Visual Node System

No code to write: you build your game logic with visual blocks (nodes) connected together. {nb_noeuds} ready-to-use nodes cover movement, physics, animation, sound, dialogues, inventory, camera, timers and conditions. Collapse whole chains of nodes to keep your workspace clear. One button tidies up all the nodes in a single tap, into readable left-to-right trees.
Yop2D node settings window
The Brain of Your Games

Tap a node to set it up: the window first shows what it acts on (① On what?), then its settings (②). Pick images, sounds or animations from lists, and answer "yes" or "no" with a tap. Small formulas like score + 1 use variables, finger position, the joystick, time or object properties: just tap a helper on the left, and an "In plain words" line explains the formula in words.
Example games made with Yop2D running on Android
Example games included

Thirteen example games can be downloaded from the engine's "Examples" tab: Neon shooter (ship arcade), Neon jump (platformer with a following camera), Platformer (coins, enemies and 3 lives), Climb & run (a character that walks, jumps, crouches and climbs ladders on its own), Maze chase (a maze where two flies chase you), Pirate battle (a naval battle against pirates), Candy match (match 3 candies), Memory cards (find the matching pairs of cards), Nexus UI (a futuristic interface: menus, options, shop), Firefly Night (a choice story with 4 endings), Dungeon walk and Dungeon escape (an isometric dungeon to explore, then escape), Lost on the moon (a choice-based story in 9 languages) and a showcase of every visual effect. Open them, play them, then change them to understand how everything works. See all examples →
Yop2D editor running on an Android phone in landscape mode
On Tablets and Phones

Tablets offer the most comfortable experience, but Yop2D also runs on Android phones in landscape mode. On small screens, the panels switch to a compact layout to leave as much room as possible for your scene. The top bar scrolls with your finger and pinch zoom follows your fingers.

cartes: No-code visual nodes
{nb_noeuds} nodes to build your game logic by connecting blocks, with simple formulas when you need them.
37 beginner templates
A "Templates" tab with small projects sorted by category: each one shows a single thing and explains which node does what.
Dialogue games (visual novels)

Choice stories like with Ren'Py, but with no code and on a tablet: characters with emotions who blink and talk, text letter by letter, shaking or wavy words, big choice buttons (timed or locked), the player's name, history, 9 languages.
A real, complete visual novel

Title screen with "Continue", autosave at every line and 5 save slots with a picture, a ◀ Back button (even before a choice), endings to discover and a gallery of souvenir pictures, player settings (text speed, volumes, skip only what was already read), friendship hearts, a portrait in the text box, lines read aloud, choices as big illustrated cards, and a map of the whole story in the editor. The buttons fold into a single ☰ menu.
Atmospheres, zoom and transitions
One node for rain, storms with lightning and thunder, snow, petals, fireflies, night, sunset or memories, with their sounds. Smooth zoom and circle, star or wipe transitions: for every game.
Your first game in 5 minutes
A built-in guide walks you through making a real little game step by step: try the game, add a node, connect it, set it up. At each step the engine shows you where to tap.
My animated hero and 4 missions

A 2nd built-in guide creates a hero who runs and jumps, with a ground, a background and music. Then 4 step-by-step missions continue in the same game: coins and a score, a patrolling enemy, a "Victory!" screen with confetti and sound, and finally the APK file to install on the phone. A bubble shows where to tap, and "✨ Do it for me" helps if you get stuck.
My first story in 5 minutes

A 4th built-in guide has you write a short choice story without importing anything or placing anything in the scene: a line by Hana, a question, two answers, then you play. At each step a frame shows where to tap, even inside windows.
Settings in plain words

A node's window first shows what it acts on, then its settings. Ready-to-tap helpers (finger and screen, joystick, time, objects, variables) and an "In plain words" line that turns each formula into a sentence. Simple names everywhere: "yes / no" instead of true / false.
Offline APK export
Your game becomes a real Android app, built on the tablet or phone itself, even without internet.
Scenes as objects (prefabs)
Any scene can be placed as an object inside another scene: perfect for a row of identical enemies or reusable pieces.
Tag targeting
Give objects a tag, and one node acts on all of them at once: move every enemy, destroy every coin.
Ready-made behaviors

In the "⚙ Object behavior" window, say what an object is: scenery, ground, falling object, platform character (walk, jump, ladders), top-down character or object dragged with a finger. Its animations (idle, walk, jump, climb) change on their own with the movement. Gravity, bounces, collisions, and "chase" or "flee" for enemies. An enemy can also patrol on its own: it walks back and forth, turning around at the edge of a drop or against a wall.
Pathfinding
A character or an enemy finds the shortest path on a grid by itself, going around walls: mazes, dungeons, strategy games.
Tilemaps
Paint levels from a tileset and mark solid tiles once: collisions are automatic.
Grids and puzzles
Nodes to fill a grid, match 3 identical pieces and shuffle the board: everything you need for a match-3 game like Candy match.
Isometric view
Objects go in front of or behind each other depending on their position, and the joystick follows the diagonals: perfect for dungeons and three-quarter view games like Dungeon walk.
Variables, inventory & saving
Score, lives, inventory lists, and saving or restoring the game state at any time.
Touch controls
Virtual joysticks, buttons and HUD overlays, with multi-touch: move and jump at the same time.
Pause & slow motion
The whole game follows pause and slow motion, while your pause menu keeps working.
Dialogue, sound and camera
Text dialogue, sound effects with volume control, looping music, a camera that follows the player within the level limits, camera shake and vibration.
Particles and visual effects
13 particle presets (explosion, fire, smoke, rain, snow, hyperspace, shockwave…), trails, glow, electrocution, hit stop, flash, tint, vignette and screen fade.
Games in several languages
Write each dialogue in several languages: the game automatically shows the language of the player's phone, or the one chosen in a menu.
A simple, comfortable editor

A toolbar cut down to the essentials (a single + button for objects and scenes), a clean style where only the active tool lights up in blue, a full color picker, a large window for writing texts, animations picked folder by folder, and a "move only" mode to tidy up nodes without breaking links.
A clear Inspector
The selected object shows its thumbnail and name, a padlock to lock it, collapsible sections, sliders for opacity and rotation, and a chain to keep proportions when resizing.
Built-in Yop2D library

No need to hunt for images elsewhere: about 420 images sorted by theme (characters, enemies, objects, floors, backgrounds, buttons), many of them animated ("With its animations" sets everything up), sound effects and music, 10 fonts and ready-made titles. The "Packs to download" tab adds online packs (Pirates, Space, Hologram interface, Special effects, Plane, Monsters, Touch gestures).
Discover the editor

A 3rd built-in guide explains the interface: pick and move an object, resize and rotate it, lock it, undo, move the view and zoom. A card shows where to tap and turns almost transparent when you touch the scene.
Choose your language
At first launch, a window offers the 9 languages, with the phone's language already selected. Every text in the engine is translated, error messages and APK export included.
Objects sorted into folders

In the scene's object list, create folders and subfolders and drag your objects into them with your finger. Choice lists (node target, variables, parent) follow this order, along with tags and kinds of objects: no more endless lists.
Crisp pixel art
A game setting keeps pixels perfectly sharp when you enlarge pixel art images. The Prehistoric and Ninja packs of the library are made for it.

ecole.intro: Yop2D is designed for learning by creating. Children can use it from about 8 years old with an adult (parent or teacher), and on their own from 11-12. In class, each student creates their own game on a simple tablet.
cartes: 🔒 No personal data
No account, no e-mail, no ads, nothing to buy. Statistics are anonymous and can be turned off with one tap.
📶 Works without internet
Once installed, Yop2D works offline: handy in a classroom without Wi-Fi.
📱 On school tablets
Android 7 or newer, even on entry-level devices. No computer needed.
🌍 9 languages
The interface and the games exist in 9 languages: also ideal for a foreign language class.
🧭 Step-by-step learning
"Your first game in 5 minutes", 37 templates that each show one single thing, guided missions and settings explained in plain words.
🎓 School mode
An even simpler interface, without violent content (explosions, weapons) and without links to social networks, protected by a teacher code.
mode_etapes: On the start screen, tap the 🎓 button next to "Language", turn on "School mode" and choose what changes.
Gentle content: explosions, weapons and shooting disappear from the library, along with fighting examples and templates and the "Shoot an object" node.
Simplified interface: only about fifty basic nodes (move, jump, variables, texts, sounds, conditions, scenes…) and no advanced tools.
No external links: no Discord, no Telegram, no packs to download.
The teacher chooses a 4-digit code: it is asked to change or turn off school mode. After a wrong code, you have to wait 30 seconds. The code stays on the tablet, nothing is sent.
ecole.mode_note: Projects already started keep working: school mode only changes what is offered.
ecole.enseignant_titre: Are you a teacher? Let's build Yop2D together
ecole.enseignant_texte: A quiz on today's lesson, an interactive story, an English vocabulary game… Tell us what your class needs: we can prepare templates for your lessons, add a language or a feature, and answer your questions. Yop2D is made by an independent developer who reads every message.

comparatif.choisir_titre: Yop2D is made for you if…
choisir: you only have an Android tablet or phone, and no computer;
you want to create anywhere, even without internet;
you don't want to learn a programming language;
you want a free tool with no ads, no subscription and no watermark in your games;
you want to write a choice story (visual novel) without learning a script, and maybe mix in a real game (puzzles, platforms, fights);
you want to share your games as Android apps with friends, family or students.
limites: Your games run on Android only: no iPhone, web or computer version.
No AAB export yet, the format required to publish on Google Play. It is planned for a later version.
It is a young engine, in testing: the community and the number of tutorials are still small, and bugs are possible.

questions: What is Yop2D?

Yop2D is a free, no-code 2D game engine for Android. It lets anyone create a complete video game on a tablet or phone with visual nodes, without programming knowledge, and export it as an APK directly on the device.
Is Yop2D really free? Are there ads?
Yes, Yop2D is 100% free: no subscription, no in-app purchases, no hidden fees. There are no ads in Yop2D, and there never will be.
Who owns the games I make? Can I sell them?
Your games belong to you. You can keep them, give them away, share them or sell them, without asking permission and without paying anything to Yop2D.
Can I make a visual novel, like with Ren'Py?

Yes. Yop2D has nodes made for dialogue games: "Say a line" (character, emotion, text letter by letter), "Ask a choice" (one output per answer, timer, locked answers), "Change the background", "Ask the player for a text" (their name) and "Atmosphere" (rain, storm, snow, night…). Characters have a sheet with one picture per emotion; they blink and talk. Everything is done with your finger, no code, and the game can be in 9 languages. Open the "Choice story" template or the Firefly Night example to start. There is also a title screen with "Continue", autosave and 5 save slots, the ◀ Back button, endings to discover with a gallery, player settings, friendship hearts, read-aloud and a map of the whole story. The "My first story" guide shows how to start in 5 minutes.
Is there a Yop2D logo or watermark in my games?
No. The games you export contain no Yop2D logo, splash screen or watermark.
Is Yop2D open source?
No. Yop2D is free to use, but its source code is not public. This changes nothing for your games: they are entirely yours.
I don't know how to code. Is that a problem?

Not at all. Yop2D replaces code with visual nodes that you connect together. It is made for beginners and for creators who prefer to focus on their game. The beginner guides show you how, step by step.
Which devices does Yop2D run on?

Android tablets and phones with Android 7.0 or newer. Tablets are the most comfortable; on phones, Yop2D works in landscape mode with a compact interface. There is no version for iPhone, iPad or computer.
Do I need a computer or an internet connection?
No. Yop2D creates and exports your game as a standalone APK directly on your device, 100% offline. No cloud build, no account.
Can I publish my game on Google Play?

Not directly yet. Yop2D exports APK files: you can install them, share them, or publish them on sites that accept APKs, such as itch.io. Google Play requires the AAB format signed with your own key: this export is planned for a later version.
Can I play my Yop2D game on iPhone, on the web or on a computer?
No. Games made with Yop2D are Android apps. If you need other platforms, see the comparison for engines that support them.
What kinds of games can I make?

2D games: platformers, top-down adventures, shooters, arcade and puzzle games, quizzes, interactive stories… The tile editor, physics, collisions, animations, dialogues, inventory and saving cover most needs. Yop2D does not make 3D games.
Can I use my own images, sounds and music?

Yes. You import your own images, tilesets, animation frames, sound effects and music. Titles and text effects are created directly in the engine. The engine also includes a library of about 420 images (many animated), sound effects, music, fonts and ready-made titles, plus packs to download: no need to look elsewhere to get started.
What languages is Yop2D available in?
The interface, the built-in help, the guides and the node reference are available in 9 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.
How do I learn to use Yop2D?

Start with the "Your first game in 5 minutes" guide: it has you build a real little game step by step, showing you where to tap. Open the "Templates" tab: 37 small projects that each show a single thing, with an explanation on screen. Then play with the fourteen example games and follow the beginner guides. The node reference explains all {nb_noeuds} nodes, and the YouTube channel, Discord and Telegram are there to help. In the engine, the "My animated hero" guide and its 4 step-by-step missions (☰ → Step-by-step missions) go even further, all the way to the game installed on your phone. The "Discover the editor" guide explains the interface: move, resize, rotate, lock, undo.
How do I resume a mission halfway through?

Open your project, tap ☰ then "Step-by-step missions" and choose the mission. The bubble starts again from the first step: tap "Skip" to jump over the steps you've already done, or "◀" to go back to a previous step. A finished mission shows a ✓ and can be done again.
Why does Android show a warning when I install the APK?
Because the APK is downloaded outside the Play Store. Tap More details, then Install anyway. You can also join the closed test on Google Play: how to become a tester.
Does Yop2D collect data?

Yop2D sends anonymous usage statistics: when it is opened and closed, how long it was used, and crash reports (type of error only), with the app version, Android version and device language. The country is estimated from the connection, without storing the IP address. No personal data and nothing from your projects. You can turn it off on the home screen, and the games you export send nothing. Details: privacy policy.
Is Yop2D finished?

Yop2D is in active development and in closed testing on Google Play. It is already usable to make complete games, but bugs are possible: export your projects regularly as a backup, and report problems on Discord or Telegram.
Who makes Yop2D?
Yop2D is made by an independent developer, with the feedback of its community of testers.
How is Yop2D different from GDevelop, Construct or Godot?

Yop2D is designed to work entirely on an Android tablet or phone, without code, without internet and without a computer, and it stays free with no ads. In return, it only makes 2D games for Android. See the detailed comparison.
Can Yop2D be used in class?

Yes. Yop2D is free, with no ads, no account and no personal data, and it works offline on ordinary Android tablets. School mode (the 🎓 button on the start screen) simplifies the interface, hides violent content and external links, and is protected by a teacher code. Teachers can write to us to adapt Yop2D to their class.
Is Yop2D suitable for children?

Yes, from about 8 years old with an adult (parent or teacher), and on their own from 11-12. The built-in guides show where to tap, the templates explain one thing at a time and the settings are written in plain words. School mode makes the interface even simpler and gentler.
